meta.reference_resolver: tools/data/mapping_resolver.js (port this to C# in bridge.exe)
meta.confidence: Troop/scene/culture ids are VERIFIED to exist (validator). Culture->profile choices, ladders, tier rule, scene classification, scaling and casualty formulas are DESIGN (INFERRED).
culture_resolution_order: 1. culture_profile_map[ck3 culture key] when the bridge knows the key (all 244 template cultures)
3. heritage_profile_map[heritage]  (hybrid/divergent cultures keep a parent heritage)
maa_resolution_order: 2. ov = maa_overrides[key]; tier = ov.tier_target ?? maa_tier[key].tier_target (+ maa_tier[key].terrain_tier_delta[terrain]) ; unknown key -> base_roles[base_type].ref_tier
3. ladder = shared_ladders[ov.ladder_ref] || maa_ladders[role][ov.force_culture || base_roles[bt].force_culture] || profile.role_overrides[role] (era-gated) || maa_ladders[role][profile.bl_culture]
4. troops = interpolate(ladder, tier); agent_multiplier = clamp(2^((tier - ladder_max)/2), 1, 2) above the top rung, clamp(2^((tier - ladder_min)/2), 0.5, 1) below the bottom rung

heritage_israelite|western_unit_gfx.why: Ashkenazi live in the Holy Roman Empire and CK3 draws them with western gfx.

heritage_latin|eastern_unit_gfx.why: Roman (restored Roman culture) uses eastern/Byzantine gfx.

heritage_tai|mongol_unit_gfx.why: Tujia (Hunan/Hubei hills) use mongol gfx in CK3 but live inside the Chinese sphere.

default.label: Fallback (no rule matched)
default.why: Empire has all four formation classes incl. crossbows and horse archers, so it is the safest generic medieval army.

western_feudal.label: Frankish / German / English / Italian / Gothic feudal
western_feudal.why: Vlandia is the Norman/Western feudal faction: couched-lance knights, crossbows, spear/billmen. CK3 draws all of these with western_unit_gfx.

iberian_christian.label: Christian Iberia
iberian_christian.why: Feudal knights like the rest of the West (vlandia), but Iberian light horse were jinetes with javelins and the almogavars were javelin infantry, so light cavalry and skirmishers come from the Aserai javelin lines.

andalusian.label: al-Andalus
andalusian.why: iberian_muslim_unit_gfx; Andalusi armies were Arab-Berber in kit (Aserai), with Western-style crossbows.

norse.label: Norse / Scandinavian
norse.why: Sturgia is Bannerlord's Rus/Viking faction (Varyag, Line Breaker, Heroic Line Breaker = berserker/ulfhednar). Viking-age nobles fought on foot, so knights are foot huscarls until the High Medieval era. The Viking-age extras (Skolderbrotva raiders, berserkers) end with the Early Medieval era (restricted_troops).

east_slavic.label: Rus / East Slavic
east_slavic.why: Sturgia is modelled on Kievan Rus (druzhina, lamellar, round shields).

west_slavic.label: Polish / Czech / Wendish
west_slavic.why: Early West Slavs fought like the Rus (sturgia). From the High Medieval era Polish and Bohemian nobles were Western-style knights, so heavy cavalry and knights switch to Vlandia.

balkan.label: South Slavic / Vlach / Albanian
balkan.why: Bulgarian and Serbian states copied the Byzantine military (empire MaA, cataphract-style nobles) while the peasant levy was Slavic (sturgia levy). CK3 draws them with eastern_unit_gfx (Byzantine models).

byzantine.label: Greek / Roman
byzantine.why: The Calradic Empire is Bannerlord's Byzantium: legionaries, menavliatons, cataphracts, bucellarii.

caucasian.label: Armenian / Georgian
caucasian.why: Armenian azatani and Georgian monaspa were Byzantine-style heavy cavalry (empire); their mounted archers looked Near-Eastern, so archer cavalry comes from the Aserai mamluk line.

arab.label: Arab / Levantine / Egyptian / Syriac / Jewish (mena)
arab.why: Aserai are Bannerlord's Arab faction (faris, mamluks, desert kit).

berber.label: Berber / Guanche / Zaghawa
berber.why: Aserai kit; Berber armies leaned on javelin light horse and javelin infantry (Jawwal, Beni Zilal minor factions).

east_african.label: Ethiopian / Nubian / Somali / Swahili
east_african.why: mena_unit_gfx in CK3; Aserai bodies and light kit are the closest Bannerlord look. Levies are foot (spears, javelins, bows).

sahel.label: Sahel / Mande / Senegambia / Kanem-Hausa
sahel.why: Sahelian empires (Ghana, Mali, Kanem, Jolof, Mossi) fielded Muslim-style mailed cavalry and archers; Aserai (faris, mamluks) is the closest look and has darker body templates than any European faction.

african_forest.label: Akan / Yoruba / Edo / Igbo
african_forest.why: Forest-belt states fought almost entirely on foot (archers, javelins, swords). Aserai bodies, foot-only levy, foot elite knights.

persian.label: Iranian / Tocharian / Brahui
persian.why: No Iranian faction exists. Persianate armies (Samanid, Buyid, Ghaznavid, Seljuk ghulams) were Near-Eastern heavy horse archers, faris-like aswaran and Daylamite infantry; the Aserai mamluk line matches that look better than the Roman-looking Empire.

steppe.label: Turkic / Mongolic / Hunnic / Tungusic
steppe.why: Khuzait are Bannerlord's Turko-Mongol steppe faction (horse archers, lancers, kheshig). Nomadic governments switch to the mounted levy variant. Their horse archers also field the Karakhergit nomads, a steppe minor faction kept out of the other Khuzait-based profiles.

hungarian.label: Hungarian (settled Magyar)
hungarian.why: Magyar horse archery survives as hussars/horse archers (khuzait), but the Christian kingdom had foot levies and, from the High Medieval era, Western-style knights.

tibetan.label: Tibetan / Qiangic (Tangut)
tibetan.why: Tibetan Empire and Tangut armies were lamellar-armoured lancers and archers from a pastoral plateau: Khuzait kit, but levies mostly on foot.

east_asian.label: Chinese / Korean / Viet / Hmong (chinese_unit_gfx)
east_asian.why: No Chinese faction exists. Khuzait lamellar, spears and horse archers are the closest East-Asian look; Song/Tang/Goryeo crossbow corps use the Empire crossbow line (also lamellar). Levies are foot.

japanese.label: Japanese / Ryukyuan
japanese.why: Early samurai were lamellar-armoured mounted archers (khuzait noble line: kheshig, khan's guard). Naginata/yari foot use the Empire menavliaton (polearm) line.

emishi.label: Emishi / Ainu
emishi.why: Emishi were famed mounted archers (CK3 emishi_horse_archers); Khuzait mixed levy with horse archers.

siberian.label: Nivkh
siberian.why: Amur/Sakhalin hunter-fishers: foot archers and spearmen with East-Asian bodies (khuzait foot + Vakken forest archers).

indian.label: Indo-Aryan / Dravidian (indian_unit_gfx)
indian.why: No Indian faction exists. Aserai turbans, light mail, bow-armed foot and faris-style cavalry are the closest look and body templates. Elephants are handled per MaA (heavy-cavalry substitute).

southeast_asian.label: Burman / Mon-Khmer / Tai / Austronesian
southeast_asian.why: Infantry-heavy tropical armies; Aserai light kit and darker bodies are the least-bad fit. Nobles fought on elephants or on foot, so knights mix faris and foot guards.

baltic_finnic.label: Baltic / Finnic / Volga-Finnic / Ugro-Permian (northern_unit_gfx)
baltic_finnic.why: Northern forest peoples next to the Rus: Sturgian kit, plus the Vakken "forest people" minor faction (Bannerlord's Finno-Ugric-inspired archers) for bows.

celtic.label: Brythonic / Goidelic
celtic.why: Battania is Bannerlord's Celtic faction (falxmen, oathsworn, fian longbowmen). Galloglass mercenaries join the heavy infantry from the High Medieval era (they appear in Ireland in the 13th century).

levy_rules.variant: profiles[p].levy_variant; if the army owner has government_has_flag = government_is_nomadic and the profile bl_culture is khuzait, use steppe_nomadic
levy_rules.tier: levy_era_tier[army owner culture era]; same tier scale as MaA (10/10 levy vs armored_footmen 32/22 = tier 1.2)
levy_rules.note: CK3 levies are generic 10/10 soldiers with no culture variant; the variant only changes the look and the melee/ranged/mounted shares.

tier_rule.note: per-soldier CK3 damage/toughness relative to the regular reference MaA of the same base type; terrain/winter bonuses give tier deltas (applied on top of overrides too)
tier_rule.terrain_delta_rule: tier += clamp(terrain_tier_delta[terrain] + winter_tier_delta[winter], -1.5, +1.0); a large malus (e.g. light cavalry in wetlands) then also lowers agent_multiplier below the bottom rung
tier_rule.agent_multiplier: tier above the ladder top -> extra agents 2^((tier-top)/2) capped 2.0; tier below the bottom rung -> fewer agents 2^((tier-bottom)/2) floored 0.5

elephant_cavalry.note: no elephants in Bannerlord: heavy cavalry substitute, tier measured against armored_horsemen

gunpowder.note: no single-player firearms: crossbow substitute; ref crossbowmen sits at tier 4.6 on the archer scale

siege_weapon.note: fights_in_main_phase = no for all 9 siege MaA: never spawned in a field battle

huscarl.why: Hird housecarls (Norse/Anglo-Danish): Sturgian heavy axemen and the legacy "Huskarl Swordsman" troop, whatever the owner culture.

varangian_veterans.why: Norse/Rus veterans of Miklagard with Dane axes: Sturgian Varyag / Line Breaker kit.

varangian_guards.why: Imperial Varangian Guard is Norse/Rus/English even when the owner is Greek, so the Sturgian axe line is used regardless of culture.

praetorian.why: Revived Roman legionaries (legionnaires innovation / Hellenic holy order): Imperial Legionary.

druzhina.why: Rus retinue infantry; Sturgia's heavy infantry line is literally modelled on the druzhina.

order_serjeants.why: Serjeant-brothers of the Catholic military orders: Vlandian sergeants.

samurai.why: Foot samurai with naginata/yari: Imperial menavliaton (polearm) and Khuzait lamellar spearmen.

zhanmadao_infantry.why: Song "horse-cutting saber" two-handed infantry: polearm/two-handed heavy foot.

landsknecht.why: German pike and zweihander mercenaries: Vlandian pikemen + Hired Pike.

picchieri.why: Italian communal pikemen: Vlandian pike line.

schiltron.why: Scottish pike rings: real pikes (Hired Pike, Vlandian Pikeman) mixed with Battanian spearmen for the look.

longbowmen.why: CK3 longbowmen have low per-man stats (20/8) but counter heavy cavalry and skirmishers (counters cut the target's damage by up to 90%, MEN_AT_ARMS_MAX_COUNTER 0.9). Bannerlord can only express that through stronger long bows, so the tier is raised to 4.5 on the long-bow ladder (Battanian highborn/fian + Brotherhood of the Woods).

crossbowmen.why: Crossbow MaA use the crossbow ladder.

shenbigong.why: Song "divine arm bow" is a heavy crossbow.

rocket_carts.why: Fire-arrow carts: no artillery in a field mission, represented as a heavy missile volley (crossbows).

metsanvartija.why: Finnic "forest guardians": Vakken forest-people archers (Bannerlord's Finno-Ugric minor faction).

jomsviking_pirates.why: Elite Norse mercenaries (30/30): Skolderbrotva/Lakepike and Sturgian heavy axemen.

caballero.why: Iberian caballeros villanos / jinetes: javelin light horse (Aserai tribal horsemen, Beni Zilal).

mulaththamun.why: Almoravid veiled Berber cavalry: the Berber javelin light horse (Beni Zilal) whatever the owner culture.

ayrudzi.why: Armenian noble horsemen (50/30, stack 50) are armoured lancer-archers, closer to heavy cavalry than to scouts.

cataphract.why: Byzantine kataphraktoi. The formula gives 4.32 (125/35 is only 25% above armored_horsemen per soldier), but Bannerlord has a troop literally named Imperial Cataphract at T5, so the tier is pinned to 5 for recognisability; the power gap is small.

order_knights.why: Templar/Hospitaller brother-knights were dedicated professional knights; CK3 rates them 112/36 at stack 50 (top per-man heavy cavalry), so they use the Vlandian noble knight line at tier 5.

tiefutu.why: Jurchen "iron pagoda" lancers: Khuzait heavy lancers.

cataphract_archers.why: Armoured horse archers (Khans of the Steppe): Khuzait heavy horse archers / kheshig.

kheshig.why: Mongol imperial guard: Khuzait Kheshig / Khan's Guard.

japanese_horse_archers.why: Mounted samurai (yumi + lamellar o-yoroi): Khuzait noble horse archers.

camel_rider.why: Only native camel riders are the Jawwal (light) and Ghilman (heavy) minor factions; used for every culture.

war_elephant.why: No elephant monster/item exists in Bannerlord 1.4.8. Substitute: the culture's heaviest cavalry at the computed tier (250/50 per man is about an accolade lancer); any tier above the ladder top is converted into extra agents (agent_multiplier).

accolade_maa_elephantiers.why: Elephant accolade (400/100): heavy cavalry substitute at the ladder top plus extra agents for the tier overflow.

ballista_elephant.why: Elephant-mounted ballista: heavy horse archers substitute (mobile missile platform).

handgunners.why: No firearms are used by any single-player item in 1.4.8: heavy crossbowmen substitute.

nomadic_riders.why: Nomad herd riders: low-tier Khuzait horse archers (tribal warriors).

restricted_troops.note: Troops matching a pattern resolve only where an allow entry matches (profile/MaA/shared ladder/use/era); allow [] = never. Checked by CK3xBL.Mapping.Data.TroopRestrictions at load.

rules.what: Brotherhood of the Woods: Vlandian forest outlaws with long bows

allow.why: English and Welsh longbowmen (longbowmen MaA): the yeoman look
Baltic, Finnic and Siberian forest peoples
Jomsviking mercenaries are Norse whoever hires them

rules.what: Ghilman: Darshi slave soldiers, heavy camel rider at tier 3

allow.why: Gaelic heavy infantry from the 13th century

rules.what: Eleftheroi: unarmoured highland lancers of a Calradian minor faction
Legion of the Betrayed: renegade legionaries (hastati/principes/triarii)
Hidden Hand: slingers and knife throwers of a secret society
Embers of the Flame: robed religious zealots
Company of the Boar: a named Vlandian crossbow company
Sword Sisters: quest and arena women
Sturgian brigand line (regular Sturgian skirmishers and light horse, bandit-named)

allow.why: profiles built on Sturgia (troop trees or levies)

rules.what: Caravan guards and masters: civilian caravan crew
Sturgian Heroic Line Breaker: wolf-skin berserker

knight_rules.agents: each CK3 knight = 1 named hero agent (always, never scaled) + retinue agents
knight_rules.retinue: retinue = min(10, round(max(0, (2.236 * prowess * scale * (1 + knight_effectiveness_mult) - 4) / 4)))  # knight power in levy units = sqrt(50p/10 * 10p/10) = 2.236p; one tier-5/6 agent ~ 4 levy agents
knight_rules.troop_source: profile.knights (era-gated) else knights[bl_culture]; retinue uses the same list
knight_rules.prowess_phase1: hero agent health multiplier = clamp(1 + prowess/25, 1, 3) applied at spawn (Agent.Health/HealthLimit)
knight_rules.prowess_phase2: CK3Bridge NPCCharacters ck3b_knight_<bl_culture>_p<band> with weapon/riding/athletics skills = clamp(60 + 8*prowess, 60, 330), bands 0-4,5-9,10-14,15-19,20-29,30+

fate.downed_not_killed_side_lost: capture with p = 0.35: <enemy side_primary_participant> = { imprison = { target = <knight> type = dungeon } } (verify imprison type keys); otherwise wounded

commander_rules.body: commanders[bl_culture][male_mounted|male_foot|female]; a female CK3 commander keeps her gender first: no female body in the culture -> female body of female_fallback[bl_culture]; an empty male slot -> the other male slot of the same culture
commander_rules.must_add_as_character: CustomBattleCombatant.GetTacticsSkillAmount() takes the max Tactics over _characters, so the general must be AddCharacter()ed as well as SetGeneral() (CustomBattleHelper does the same)
commander_rules.martial_to_tactics: Bannerlord field-battle AI unlocks tactics by side max Tactics: <20 Charge only; >=20 FullScaleAttack + DefensiveEngagement/DefensiveLine (def) or RangedHarrassmentOffensive (att); >=50 FrontalCavalryCharge + DefensiveRing/HoldChokePoint (def) or CoordinatedRetreat (att). Map CK3 martial m -> Tactics = clamp(10*m, 0, 300): m<=1 charge-only, m 2-4 basic, m>=5 full set. Needs phase-2 custom commander characters; stock bodies have Tactics 15 (commander_12/24) to 200.
commander_rules.advantage: adv = martial + terrain defender_advantage (defender only) + 5 for the defender in harsh winter (winter_harsh_modifier: defender_winter_advantage = 5) + commander-trait advantage for the terrain/winter; delta = adv_A - adv_B; the side ahead deals outgoing damage x (1 + 0.025*|delta|) capped at +30% (CK3 default game rule is +5%/point; halved because Bannerlord melee already snowballs). Implement in a CK3Bridge AgentApplyDamageModel registered in SubModule.OnGameStart (CustomGame calls GameManager.OnGameStart after its own models).
commander_rules.morale: initial morale + |delta| (max +15) for the side ahead

scaling.max_total_agents_rule: both sides incl. reinforcements; default 1.5 x BannerlordConfig.GetRealBattleSize() (battle sizes 200..1000 on the field), user-configurable
scaling.scale: s = min(1, (max_total_agents - hero_agents) / (field_soldiers_attacker + field_soldiers_defender))  # same s for both sides keeps the side ratio
scaling.field_soldiers: levies + every MaA regiment maa_current_troops_count except siege_weapon (fights_in_main_phase = no)
scaling.regiment_agents: agents_i = max(1, round(n_i * s * agent_multiplier_i)) for n_i > 0; levy pool absorbs rounding (largest-remainder over the side)
scaling.ratio_guard: after minimums, if a side ratio differs from the CK3 soldier ratio by >5%, shrink that side's levy pool (never below 0) until within 5%
scaling.hero_agents: commanders (1 each, every army commander on the side) + knights (1 each) + knight retinues; not scaled
scaling.group_tracking: every agent must carry its CK3 group id (regiment / levy pool / knight): CK3Bridge supplies its own IMissionTroopSupplier/IAgentOriginBase; fallback = split losses of a shared troop id proportionally to spawned counts

fatal_ratio_modifiers.rule: fatal_ratio = 0.3 x (1 + side terrain hard_casualty_modifier) x (1.2 in harsh winter); pursuit q x (1 + loser retreat_losses) (wetlands +0.25 both sides, desert_mountains defender -0.3). Values VERIFIED from common/terrain_types/00_terrains.txt via ck3_catalog; applying them this way is INFERRED.

casualties.ck3_model: Routed casualties return to the army after battle; fatal casualties are permanent (game_concepts_l_english.yml:972-975). Main phase converts BASE_RATIO_CASUALTIES_CONVERSION = 0.3 of casualties to fatal; the pursuit (aftermath) turns routed into fatal: 5% of routed toughness (BASE_TOUGHNESS_TO_PURSUIT) + 0.5 x pursuit (PURSUIT_STAT_TO_PURSUIT_DAMAGE) minus screen, at least 1% (MINIMUM_PURSUIT_DAMAGE).
casualties.bl_default: CustomGame registers DefaultAgentDecideKilledOrUnconsciousModel which returns death probability 1.0, so every downed agent is Killed unless a mission behaviour implements IAgentStateDecider
casualties.recommended_bl_model: CK3Bridge IAgentStateDecider: regular agents Killed with p = 0.3 (= CK3 main-phase conversion), heroes per knight_rules.fate
per_group: f_down = (killed + unconscious) / agents_spawned ; casualties = round(f_down * soldiers)
fatal_main = round(casualties * 0.3)   (or round(killed/agents * soldiers) when the decider is installed)
winner: fatal = fatal_main ; routed = casualties - fatal_main return to the army

loser: routed_pool = casualties - fatal_main + round(fled_agents/agents * soldiers) ; q = clamp(0.05 + 0.5 * max(0, P_win - S_lose) / T_routed, 0.01, 1.0) ; fatal = fatal_main + round(routed_pool * q)
loser annihilated (no agent fled or standing at mission end): fatal = casualties (early-phase defeat rule, ck3.paradoxwikis.com/Warfare)
P_win = sum over winner surviving MaA soldiers of pursuit (levies 0) ; S_lose = sum over loser surviving MaA soldiers of screen ; T_routed = sum routed soldiers x toughness (levy 10)

writeback.levies: army = { deplete_army_by_percentage = <fatal_levy / army_size> } THEN reset every MaA regiment of that army to its exact target with change_maa_troops_count (handles both possible deplete semantics; verify with a probe first)
writeback.winner: combat_side = { force_win = yes } on the Bannerlord winner + loser side { set_skip_pursuit = yes } so CK3 does not add its own pursuit on top of ours; alternative set_winner = yes keeps CK3's pursuit (its internal routed pool is ~0 if CK3 was paused at on_combat_start)
writeback.summary: combat_side = { battle_event = { key = ck3bl_fought_in_bannerlord left_portrait = <commander> right_portrait = <enemy commander> } } to show a line in the CK3 battle summary

terrain_scene_rules.pick: seeded random (seed = CK3 combat location province id + date) from the pool
terrain_scene_rules.pool: climate_scene_overrides[climate][terrain] if present else terrain_scenes[terrain]; is_coastal province and terrain in plains/farmlands/drylands/hills -> 30% chance coastal_scenes; is_riverside_province -> 30% chance river_scenes
terrain_scene_rules.winter_preference: season winter -> prefer pool scenes whose terrain_tags contain snow_layer (scene has a snow material layer) when the pool has any
terrain_scene_rules.culture_preference: 50% chance to restrict the pool to scenes whose culture_hint equals the Bannerlord culture of the location holder (or defender) when any exist; culture_hint/terrain_tags come from bridge/data/bl_scenes.json (name-matched Calradia settlement hints, INFERRED)
terrain_scene_rules.narrow_terrain_note: combat_width < 1 (mountains/desert_mountains 0.5, wetlands 0.6, jungle 0.7) is represented by scene choice only; defender_advantage feeds commander_rules.advantage

winter_state.source: province `has_province_modifier = winter_<x>_modifier` (game/common/modifiers/00_province_modifiers.txt:138-155; logs/triggers.log:10810). The engine swaps these modifiers as winter severity changes, so they are the authoritative winter signal; month + climate is only the fallback.

time_of_day.note: CK3 has no time of day; only 6/12/15/18/22 have atmospheres (CreateAtmosphereInfoForMission)

ck3_emit.note: ordered key lists for the generated CK3 if/else_if chains that fill request.json (CK3 script cannot print keys)

custom_troop_wishlist.why: prowess-scaled knights (skills) instead of a health multiplier
martial-scaled Tactics/Leadership so commander quality changes Bannerlord AI tactics
culture-looking camel riders (war_camel + camel_saddle with the culture kit) instead of Jawwal/Ghilman for everyone
these cultures lack horse archers; today neutral Outriders / Khuzait troops stand in
these cultures lack crossbowmen; today neutral Hired Crossbows stand in
body templates for profiles without a matching faction (West/East African, Indian, SE Asian, Chinese, Japanese)
bandits.xml is Campaign-only; peasant armies and event troops need CustomGame-loaded stand-ins

maa_base_note: maa_base[base][bl_culture] = resolver output for the typical MaA of the base type (heavy_infantry:armored_footmen, pikemen:pikemen_unit, archers:bowmen, skirmishers:light_footmen, light_cavalry:light_horsemen, heavy_cavalry:armored_horsemen, archer_cavalry:horse_archers, camel_cavalry:camel_rider, elephant_cavalry:war_elephant, gunpowder:handgunners, nomadic_horde:nomadic_riders, peasant_militia:pikemen_militia, siege_weapon:mangonel) in a plain profile of that culture; siege_weapon is empty by design (excluded).
